title: Evaluation-normalized scalar Hom comparison for a site-perfect first variable
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with a small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $R\to S$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings on that site. Use the unbounded module-sheaf derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived change of rings $F=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $P\in D(R)$ be site-perfect: locally on every site object it is represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. For every $Q\in D(R)$ the canonical morphism
$$c_{P,Q}:F H_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_S(FP,FQ)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in both variables. Here $c_{P,Q}$ is defined by tensor-Hom adjunction as the transpose of
$$FP\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}F H_R(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(P,Q))\xrightarrow{F(\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q})}FQ,$$
using the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus this specified map preserves evaluation. No flatness of $S$ over $R$, or boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor-amplitude condition on $Q$, is assumed.

proof.text: Choose the existing universal derived scalar cochain model and normalized closed symmetric tensor presentations over R and S. The existing scalar tensor theorem supplies κ,μ with exactly the generator and K-flat counit squares required by SitePerfectScalarHomData. The independent-universe scalar monoidality theorem supplies the strong monoidal structure m with tensorator μ inverse.

Build the source RingedSiteDualityModel from its recorded tensor coherence, keeping the same closed structure, K-flat models and symmetry. Apply perfect duality for this specified presentation to obtain invertibility of its canonical tensor-dual evaluation comparison.

Turn the right-tensor adjunction into a MonoidalClosed instance by the symmetry isomorphism. Naturality in the coefficient unit and the symmetric hexagons identify the specified tensor-dual comparison, after the unit-Hom isomorphism, with MonoidalClosed.ihomUnitTensorToIhom. Its component at P is invertible. The existing proved exactPairingOfIsIso construction gives an exact dual pair; apply the existing strong-monoidal Hom comparison theorem. Expanding its curry identifies it with siteScalarHomComparison.

The inverse-transpose equation gives the displayed evaluation identity. Apply inverse transposition to both sides of the two-variable naturality equation. Naturality of the tensor isomorphism, symmetry and evaluation makes the resulting composites identical. These two equations in fact hold without perfectness.
